name: N-Bodies
miniText: NetLogo N-Bodies investigates how reciprocal inverse-square forces produce collective gravitational motion. Each particle contributes a gravitational pull on every other particle; initialization can impose symmetric positions and velocities, and the display can follow the center of mass. Provides the classical gravitational and mechanical foundation; the DOI identifies a modern translation [1]. Introduces an efficient force approximation as a comparison with direct all-pairs calculation [2]. Shows why integration structure matters for long-term gravitational dynamics [3]. Point masses and finite numerical steps omit relativity and physical collision structure; neither Barnes-Hut approximation nor a symplectic scheme is implied merely by citing those methods. The simulation illustrates the consequences of mutual interaction and sensitivity to initial configurations. Reproducing these patterns establishes rule fidelity, not empirical validation.
